title: Unveiling the Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Antidepressants: A Systematic Review of Human Studies over the Last Decade.
authors: Bleibel L, Sokołowska P, Henrykowska G, Owczarek J, Wiktorowska-Owczarek A.
figures: Changes in the main pro- and anti-inflammatory factors in depression. The red arrow represents pro-inflammatory factors and their increase in depression, while the green arrow represents anti-inflammatory factors and their decrease in depression. Created with Biorender.

Reported effects of SSRIs, SNRIs, ketamine, and esketamine on cytokine levels. Numbers in the columns indicate how many studies found an increase, decrease, or no effect/no significant effect in cytokine levels after treatment with each type of antidepressant. CRP: C-reactive protein; IL-1RA: IL-1 receptor antagonist;  TNF-α: Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha; IFN-γ: interferon gamma .
The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) [ 309 ] flowchart.
tables: The effect (decrease (↓), increase (↑), or no statistically significant effect (↔)) of antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, ketamine, and esketamine) on inflammatory and non-inflammatory factors; all studies were conducted in serum.  TNF-α: Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha; NLRP3: Nod-like receptor pyrin-containing 3; IFN-γ: interferon gamma; hsCRP: high-sensitivity C-reactive protein; MDD: major depressive
